(NASDAQ: NAGE), the global authority on NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) with a focus on the science of healthy aging, today announced that its Chief Executive Officer, Rob Fried, and Chief Financial Officer, Ozan Pamir, will participate in Canaccord Genuity’s 46th Annual Growth Conference, taking place from August 11 to 13, 2026, in Boston. For additional information on Niagen Bioscience, visit www.niagenbioscience.com . About Niagen Bioscience Niagen Bioscience, Inc. (NASDAQ: NAGE) is the global authority in healthy aging and NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) science. As a trusted pioneer of NAD+ discoveries, Niagen Bioscience ™ is dedicated to advancing healthspan through precision science and innovative NAD+-boosting solutions. The Niagen Bioscience team, composed of world-renowned scientists, works with independent investigators from esteemed universities and research institutions around the globe to uncover the full potential of NAD+. A vital coenzyme found in every cell of the human body, NAD+ declines with age and exposure to everyday lifestyle stressors. NAD+ depletion is a key contributor to age-related changes in health and vitality. Distinguished by state-of-the-art laboratories, rigorous scientific and quality protocols, and collaborations with leading research institutions worldwide, Niagen Bioscience sets the gold standard for research, quality, and innovation. There’s a better way to age. At the heart of its clinically proven product portfolio is Niagen® (patented nicotinamide riboside, or NR), the most efficient, well-researched, and high-quality NAD+ booster available. Niagen powers the Company’s consumer supplement, Tru Niagen®, the number one NAD+ boosting oral supplement in the United States† (available at www.truniagen.com ), and Niagen™ Plus, featuring pharmaceutical-grade intravenous (IV) and injectable Niagen products ( www.niagenplus.com ). Pharmaceutical-grade Niagen IV and injections are compounded and distributed by U.S. FDA-registered 503B outsourcing facilities and are available exclusively at clinics with a prescription. Under NAD Pharmaceuticals Corp., the Company’s wholly owned subsidiary focused on developing therapies for accelerated aging and rare genetic diseases, is conducting research on NB4168, a differentiated molecule. Niagen Bioscience’s robust patent portfolio protects NR and other NAD+ precursors. Niagen Bioscience maintains a website at www.niagenbioscience.com , where copies of press releases, news, and financial information are regularly published. † Based on revenue per largest U.S. e-commerce marketplace (Jan. 2025 – Dec. 2025) Niagen Bioscience Media Contact: Kendall Knysch, Senior Director of Media Relations & Partnerships 310.405.5227 kendall.knysch@niagenbio.com Niagen Bioscience Investor Relations Contact: Valter Pinto, Managing Director KCSA Strategic Communications 212.896.1254 Niagen@kcsa.com Source: Niagen Bioscience, Inc View All News

title: Hillman Announces Closing of $735 Million Term Loan B and $375 Million ABL Revolving Credit Facility
summary: Successfully extends Term Loan B maturity to 2033 and ABL maturity to 2031 CINCINNATI, July 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hillman Solutions Corp.…...
body_text: Hillman Announces Closing of $735 Million Term Loan B and $375 Million ABL Revolving Credit Facility July 22, 2026 4:30pm EDT Download as PDF Successfully extends Term Loan B maturity to 2033 and ABL maturity to 2031 CINCINNATI, July 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hillman Solutions Corp . ( Nasdaq: HLMN ) (the "Company", “Hillman Group”, or "Hillman"), a leading provider of hardware and related products, announced the closing of the refinancing of its existing credit facilities, consisting of a new $735 million senior secured Term Loan B ("Term Loan B") and a $375 million asset-based revolving credit facility ("ABL Revolver"). Proceeds from the Term Loan B were primarily used to refinance the Company's existing term loan, repay amounts outstanding under its existing revolving credit facility, and pay related fees and expenses. The Term Loan B matures in July 2033 and is currently priced at SOFR +200 basis points. The ABL Revolver, which currently has a zero balance, matures in July 2031 and is currently priced at SOFR +125 basis points. The pricing of both the Term Loan B and the ABL Revolver are consistent with the previous credit facilities. "This refinancing meaningfully extends our debt maturity profile and enhances our financial flexibility,” said Jon Michael Adinolfi, Chief Executive Officer of Hillman. "It reflects the continued strength of our business and positions us well to invest in our core operations and pursue value-creating growth opportunities. These transactions give us a capital structure that supports our long-term strategic priorities including acquisitions." Jefferies Finance LLC acted as Lead Left Arranger for the Term Loan B with U.S. Bank, BofA Securities, PNC Capital Markets LLC, and Fifth Third Bank, N.A. acting as Joint Lead Arrangers, and First Financial Bank also participating in the syndicate. U.S. Bank acted as lead arranger and administrative agent for the ABL Revolver, with Bank of America, N.A., PNC Bank N.A., and Fifth Third Bank, N.A. acting as Joint Lead Arrangers, and First Financial Bank also participating in the syndicate. About Hillman Solutions Corp. Founded in 1964 and headquartered in Cincinnati, Hillman is a leading provider of hardware and related products serving retail, pro distribution, and industrial MRO customers. Over the last 60-plus years, Hillman has built a legacy of service and growth by forming strategic partnerships with North America's leading home improvement, hardware, and farm and fleet retailers. Hillman differentiates itself from the competition with its dedicated field sales team of 1,200+ associates, direct-to-store distribution capabilities, and world class global sourcing and supply chain expertise. The company offers an extensive product portfolio of more than 111,000 SKUs, including fasteners (power screws, nuts, bolts), hardware (builder's hardware, door hardware, rope & chain, accessories), project gear & supplies (gloves, work gear, paint & cleaning sundries), and key and engraving services (key duplication, auto keys, and engraving). Hillman is committed to delivering exceptional customer service, innovative products, and dependable solutions to its customers and regularly earns vendor of the year recognition from top customers. For more information on Hillman, visit www.hillman.com. title: Kanso Worldshop’s 150-Day Working Capital Window—Built by Extending Supplier Terms with Slope
summary: With Slope, Kanso Worldshop aligned repayments to inventory sales cycles, paired 90-day installments with ~60-day supplier terms, and kept more cash in the business to make larger, better-timed inventory buys on Walmart.
body_text: Highlights ~150 days Working-capital runway (supplier terms + Slope’s 90-day plan) 90-day Repayment chosen to match inventory cycles In a Nutshell Kanso Worldshop is a multi-marketplace retailer selling across Health & Beauty, Grocery, and Toys. They needed financing that aligned with the timelines in which they sell through inventory, not 30-day card cycles. With Slope’s transparent 30/60/90-day repayment options, they chose a 90-day plan and paired it with ~60-day supplier terms, creating roughly 150 days of working-capital breathing room. That change let them place larger orders when unit economics were best—and still keep cash available to add SKUs. About Kanso Worldshop Kanso Worldshop operates on Walmart (and other marketplaces), sourcing from manufacturers and distributors and managing a broad catalog across multiple categories. Prior to getting a credit line powered by Slope, they relied on credit cards, which limited order size and forced repayments on a 30-day cadence, regardless of how fast inventory sold. Challenges Card limits and 30-day repayment cycles: Traditional cards didn’t scale to purchase larger lots when pricing was most attractive, and 30-day statements didn’t match sales cycles. Bank lines were slow or too small: Years of banking relationships still hadn’t yielded the kind of limit they needed for growth. Cash tied up at the wrong moments: Paying upfront for inventory reduced the ability to buy opportunistically or expand into adjacent SKUs. Finding a Solution with Slope Kanso connected their business bank account to Slope via a secure Plaid connection and got approved for a credit line. When they were ready to draw from the line, they saw transparent costs for 30/60/90-day repayment options on the amount they were looking to draw, and got funds deposited to their bank account to use. They selected the 90-day installment plan and used their first $10,000 draw for an inventory purchase. By pairing Slope’s 90-day repayment schedule with ~60-day supplier terms , repayments now align with revenue collected from selling the inventory. The seller also called out the user experience as “super easy and friendly”—they could see the math up front and choose the plan that fit their cash flow. “Ninety-day installments are the way to go. We can buy the right inventory and keep cash in the business while we pay it down.” ‍ – Raphael & Keishla Cabrera, Owners, Kanso Worldshop The Impact Turn 30 days into ~150 days: Extending supplier terms with Slope’s 90-day plan created a longer window to sell inventory without tying up working cash. Bigger, smarter buys: The new breathing room makes it practical to time larger orders when pricing and availability are best. Reinvest month one: On a $10K order with a 90-day plan, the first month’s outlay (~$3–3.5K) still leaves ~$6–6.5K working in the business, allowing them to keep inventory moving and test additional SKUs. Confidence from transparency: Seeing 30/60/90 options and total costs up front made decision-making faster and calmer. ‍ * Disclosure: Slope is a financial technology company, not a bank. Business-purpose loans made by Lead Bank and subject to credit approval. Application and consent to obtain personal credit report is required. Subject to minimum revenue and business requirements. Personal Guaranty may be required. Fees vary based on risk assessment and loan term. ‍

title: Performance Shipping Inc. Extends Time Charter for M/T Briolette with Aramco Trading at US$37,700 Per Day for Three Years
body_text: Athens, Greece , July 6, 2026 — Performance Shipping Inc. (NASDAQ: PSHG), (“we” or the “Company”), a global shipping company specializing in the ownership of tanker vessels, today announced that, through a separate wholly-owned subsidiary, it has extended the time charter contract with Aramco Trading Fujairah FZE, (“Aramco” or the “Charterer”), for the 2011-built, 104,588 dwt Aframax tanker vessel, M/T Briolette. The gross charter rate will be US$37,700 per day for a period of 35 months +/- 30 days at the option of the Charterer. The charter commenced in direct continuation of the existing charter on July 2, 2026, and is expected to generate approximately US$39 million of gross revenue for the minimum duration of the charter. Commenting on this charter, Andreas Michalopoulos, the Company’s Chief Executive Officer, stated: “We are pleased to further strengthen our longstanding relationship with Aramco through the direct continuation of this charter under a new three-year agreement. This marks the fourth consecutive contract we have secured with one of the world's largest integrated energy and chemicals companies, underscoring the confidence placed in our ability to consistently deliver safe, reliable, and high-quality seaborne transportation services. “With this charter now in place, our contracted revenue backlog has exceeded half a billion dollars as of mid-2026, while our remaining average time charter duration has increased to 3.2 years. Our charter coverage now exceeds 80% through the end of 2028 and remains approximately 60% in 2029, providing significant earnings visibility. “Importantly, the additional contracted employment reduces the average daily charter rate required from our remaining open days to fully cover all our expected cash obligations to effectively zero through the end of 2028, increasing to only approximately US$10,000 per day in 2029. These metrics demonstrate the strength of our prudent commercial strategy, providing us with substantial financial flexibility to meet our obligations and navigate the future with confidence.”

title: Tuya Smart Demonstrates How AI is Transforming Smart Lighting and Buildings at Light + Building 2026 | news | Tuya Smart
body_text: Frankfurt, Germany — March 8, 2026 —Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA, HKEX: 2391), a global AI cloud platform service provider, today exhibited at Light + Building 2026, the world's leading trade fair for lighting and building services technology, in Frankfurt. This year, Tuya Smart presented under the theme “Hey Tuya, Hey Brighter Life,” showcasing its innovative capabilities across AI platforms, lighting, and building technologies. Tuya also joined forces with ecosystem partners including Whale Vision, MoreSense Technology, XiongYuan Lighting, Changyou Technology, Linklite, and Golden Bright to jointly stage the Tuya Global Ecosystem Exhibition, integrating foundational AI capabilities with vertical industry scenarios and presenting developers worldwide with a new AI-driven vision of a green, intelligent, and sustainable future. Tuya’s AI Innovation Engines Accelerate Physical AI Applications AI is rapidly becoming a key force reshaping the hardware industry ecosystem. At Light + Building 2026, Tuya unveiled several AI innovation engines—including the AI Agent Development Platform, Hey Tuya, and Spatial Intelligence—designed to free developers from complex technical infrastructures and enable faster product innovation and industry upgrades. AI Agent Development Platform: Empowering Developers to Turn Ideas into Reality At the Tuya booth, visitors experienced AI toys, pet companion robots, and desktop robots naturally interacting with people. These devices are not isolated products—they all “grow” from the same platform. Tuya’s AI Agent Development Platform effectively equips devices with both a “brain” and a “nervous system.” Developers can transform ideas into intelligent hardware prototypes that can speak, see, and interact within just 15 minutes, while also supporting the full path from prototype validation to large-scale mass production. Hey Tuya: Your AI Life Assistant Hey Tuya, Tuya’s AI life assistant, is powered by the company’s self-developed Physical AI Engine (PAE). It spans key home scenarios including security guardian, energy saving, work productivity, health, companionship, and pet care. The assistant supports multi-device connectivity, short-term and long-term memory, and deep integration with the global ecosystem of “Powered by Tuya” smart devices, enabling proactive perception of the physical environment and intelligent service delivery. Tuya Spatial AI: A Zero-Code Architecture for Personalized Smart Spaces Tuya Spatial AI platform is a one-stop solution that integrates scenario-based hardware packages with software capabilities, enabling customers to rapidly plan and deploy intelligent space solutions. Its core value lies in three dimensions: • Strong scenario building capability: Developers can freely build cross-industry solutions based on core capabilities, creating a scenario SaaS application in as little as 10 minutes. • AI empowerment: The platform provides spatial agents and AI services such as full-scenario data perception and multimodal scene recognition, allowing spaces to actively sense, understand, and respond to user needs. • Open integration: Rich APIs and developer tools allow rapid development of customized applications. From Indoor to Outdoor: Using AI to Illuminate Every Inch of Space Tuya’s innovations extend beyond technology into deep insights across vertical scenarios. Leveraging strong AI capabilities, Tuya has developed comprehensive indoor and outdoor lighting solutions, showcased alongside ecosystem partners at the exhibition to deliver smarter and more comfortable lighting experiences. AI Whole-Home Lighting Solution: Let Light Move with Your Imagination This solution integrates AI scenarios, AI dimming, AI gateways, AI voice, and AI companionship to create a complete intelligent experience—from environmental perception and device linkage to voice interaction and emotional engagement. Powered by comprehensive data and AI algorithms, users can simply upload a scene photo or enter a short text description, and the system will automatically generate a matching lighting scenario. By combining proprietary hardware with open software—along with standardized APIs and complete SDKs, the solution ensures efficient and reliable project deployment. Ambient Lighting Solution: Unlock Personalized Lighting Experiences The ambient lighting solution jointly launched by Linklite and Tuya attracted significant attention at the exhibition. For indoor environments, the solution integrates an HDMI screen synchronizer with a Zigbee gateway, synchronizing wireless lighting devices with screen content to create immersive lighting effects that enhance movies, entertainment, and gaming experiences. For outdoor scenarios, Linklite combines products such as outdoor spotlights, pathway lights, string lights, and eave lights with Tuya’s ambient lighting solution to create dynamic garden lighting displays. Users can freely adjust brightness and color to match different moods and occasions, bringing outdoor spaces to life at night. Lighting Driver Solution: The Core Engine for High-Quality Lighting Efficient, safe, and intelligent power drivers are critical to lighting system performance. Tuya’s new generation smart lighting driver solution enables precise control of brightness and color temperature while significantly improving energy efficiency. This solution can be widely applied in commercial and office lighting scenarios, helping customers build energy-efficient and reliable lighting systems. XiongYuan Lighting, a global provider of advanced power solutions, showcased its upgraded smart driver power series powered by Tuya. These products feature built-in Zigbee, Bluetooth, and Matter multi-mode gateways, enabling seamless cross-gateway and cross-protocol connectivity—even under weak network or offline conditions. Smart Street Lighting Solution: Powering the Smart City At the exhibition, Golden Bright partnered with Tuya to introduce a new smart street lighting solution. The solution supports a variety of lighting systems—including high-mast lights, solar streetlights, outdoor street lamps, and high-bay lighting—and integrates Tuya’s App + SaaS management platform for street lighting. It enables on-demand lighting, fault self-diagnosis, and remote operation and maintenance, significantly reducing energy consumption and operational costs while supporting smart city infrastructure development. Tuya and Ecosystem Partners: Reimagining the Life of Buildings with AI AI technology is transforming the entire lifecycle of buildings. At Light + Building 2026, Tuya and its ecosystem partners demonstrated how AI can reconstruct every “cell” of a building—from environmental perception to intent understanding, from precise control to autonomous decision-making. Buildings are evolving from collections of smart devices into truly intelligent spaces that can breathe, think, and adapt. IPC Solution: Advancing AI Security Applications Tuya’s AI-powered IPC solution continues to evolve with new capabilities. On one hand, it supports customizable smart events and free-of-charge recognition of five common targets: people, vehicles, pets, packages, and flames. On the other hand, it enables intelligent analysis of event footage—moving from simply identifying objects to understanding entire scenarios. At the exhibition, Tuya integrated this solution with WhaleView’s wall-mounted camera lights to create a smart courtyard lighting camera solution. With a built-in high-definition wide-angle camera, the system captures critical motion even in low-light environments while utilizing human detection and motion tracking algorithms to seamlessly integrate professional security capabilities into outdoor landscape lighting. Building Electrical Solution: EnerVision AI Makes Every Kilowatt Traceable Tuya introduced a new building electrical solution powered by its self-developed EnerVision AI. The system employs the globally advanced Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) technology and supports non-destructive upgrades. Without opening walls or modifying each appliance, AI analyzes subtle current waveform changes to map energy consumption patterns of household devices—from air conditioners and refrigerators to hidden standby power usage. Based on AI algorithms, the system automatically optimizes electricity consumption strategies, reduces peak loads, and provides scientifically grounded energy-saving recommendations, making green buildings more achievable. At the exhibition, Changyou Technology integrated its circuit breakers, smart meters, multi-mode 4G gateways, and waterproof smart boxes with Tuya’s Building Environmental Management System (BEMS) to deliver refined power management and energy monitoring for lighting, sockets, air conditioning, and other building systems. Smart Sensor Solution: The “Nerve Endings” of Intelligent Buildings Tuya’s Smart Sensor Solution includes a full range of sensors—such as motion detection, light sensing, and door/window sensors—allowing flexible deployment based on scenario needs. MoreSense Technology, a leading radar sensing and IoT communication module brand, showcased its 24G human presence detection and smart commercial lighting solution together with Tuya. By collecting real-time environmental data, the system enables accurate decision-making for spatial intelligence—from energy-saving automation like lights turning on when people arrive to dynamic air-conditioning adjustments. Smart Mobility Solution: Connecting People, Vehicles, and Homes Tuya’s vision is expanding beyond static spaces to more dynamic mobility scenarios. In the mobility and wearable device exhibition area, Tuya showcased AI-powered solutions for commercial fleets, personal mobility, and even pet travel scenarios. For industry fleets, Tuya has launched the Ofstar AI Fleet integrated software and hardware solution, which integrates advanced communication, positioning, video, sensing, and AI technologies to achieve one-stop management from secure dispatching to asset protection. For personal mobility, Tuya demonstrated 4G smart vehicle control units and e-bike dashboards, enabling battery monitoring, remote control, and riding data management through the Tuya platform. These systems also support digital operations for both offline stores and online marketplaces. Meanwhile, Tuya is building a cross-scenario ecosystem connecting people, vehicles, and homes, breaking down the barriers between car systems and smart home devices so users can control home devices directly from their vehicles for seamless service integration. At Light + Building 2026, Tuya Smart presented a wide range of lighting and building solutions, delivering a comprehensive AI-driven technology showcase to developers around the world. Looking ahead, Tuya will continue to iterate on AI products and services, focusing on advancing AI capabilities and real-world applications while empowering global developers to build a greener, low-carbon, and sustainable future together.

title: Power When It Matters Most: Tesla's Free Supercharging Response to Earthquakes and Wildfires
summary: Introduction On July 28, 2026, a magnitude-7 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southwestern Japan. The same week, devastating wildfires swept across southwestern France and Spain, forcing evacuations and disrupting travel. In both cases, Tesla responded within hours. The company activated free Supercharging at s
body_text: Introduction On July 28, 2026, a magnitude-7 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southwestern Japan . The same week, devastating wildfires swept across southwestern France and Spain, forcing evacuations and disrupting travel . In both cases, Tesla responded within hours. The company activated free Supercharging at select locations across all three countries, effective from midnight July 29 through midnight August 5, 2026 . In Japan, ten Supercharger stations across five prefectures in Kyushu were made free . In France and Spain, stations in wildfire-affected regions were opened at no cost . This was not a one-off gesture. Tesla has a well-established track record of offering free Supercharging during natural disasters, extreme weather events, and humanitarian crises . From hurricanes in the United States to floods in Europe and earthquakes in Japan, the company has repeatedly leveraged its charging infrastructure as a public good. II. The Japan Earthquake Response 2.1 The Earthquake On July 28, 2026, a powerful earthquake with a maximum seismic intensity of 7 struck the Kumamoto region in southern Japan . The tremor raised widespread concerns across Kyushu, Japan's southernmost main island . The region has a history of significant seismic activity, including the devastating 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes that caused extensive damage and loss of life. Tesla's response was swift. The company's official Tesla Charging account on X announced that ten Supercharger locations across five Kyushu prefectures would be free from midnight July 29 through midnight August 5. 2.2 The Locations The ten Japanese Supercharger stations covered by the relief program are distributed across Kyushu : Kitakyushu (Fukuoka Prefecture) Fukuoka (two locations: one in the city and one in Kashiihama, Higashi-ku) Fukuoka – Hakataeki Minami Oita (Oita Prefecture) Kumamoto (Kumamoto Prefecture) Miyazaki (Miyazaki Prefecture) Kagoshima (Kagoshima Prefecture) These locations span the length of Kyushu, from Kitakyushu in the north to Kagoshima in the south, providing broad coverage for affected communities. 2.3 Tesla-Only Access in Japan Unlike the European relief effort, the Japanese Supercharger stations were opened exclusively to Tesla vehicles . The announcement made no mention of non-Tesla EV eligibility . This distinction reflects the current state of Tesla's Supercharger network in Japan, where third-party access has a more limited rollout compared to Europe . It is not a deliberate exclusion but rather a practical limitation based on the network's configuration in that market . Japanese Tesla owners in affected prefectures can use these stations at no cost during the relief period . No promo code or account change is required—the session cost simply shows as zero. III. The European Wildfire Response 3.1 Wildfires in France and Spain While Japan dealt with earthquakes, southwestern Europe faced a different emergency. Severe wildfires were burning across France and Spain, forcing evacuations and disrupting travel . In France, the Gironde department west of Bordeaux has been among the most fire-prone areas in the country for several years running . The summer of 2026 brought another devastating fire season, with communities in and around the Bordeaux region facing immediate danger. Tesla responded by activating free Supercharging at five locations in the Bordeaux area and four locations in Spain . 3.2 French Locations The five French Supercharger stations covered by the relief program are : Arès (Gironde) Biganos (Gironde) Mérignac (Gironde, near Bordeaux) Bordeaux Lac (Bordeaux) Bègles (Gironde, near Bordeaux) These locations form a tight geographic cluster around the Gironde estuary west of Bordeaux . This is not a coincidence—the concentration of stations in this area ensures that evacuees and relief workers moving through this corridor can charge without cost . 3.3 Spanish Locations In Spain, Tesla activated free Supercharging at : Castellón (Castellón province) Sagunto (Valencia province) Fuenlabrada (Madrid) Majadahonda (Madrid) These locations cover both the eastern coast near Valencia and the Madrid metropolitan area, providing relief to drivers in regions impacted by ongoing wildfire conditions . 3.4 Open to All EVs — A Significant Move Perhaps the most notable aspect of the European relief effort is that the France and Spain locations are open to all electric vehicle owners, regardless of brand . Non-Tesla EV drivers can access these stations through the Tesla app or the in-car touchscreen on CCS-compatible vehicles . Tesla has extended its network to non-Tesla EVs across much of Europe in recent years, and this relief activation leverages that existing infrastructure to maximize community impact . This decision significantly expands the reach of Tesla's disaster-response efforts. Rather than limiting free charging to Tesla owners—who are already a minority of EV drivers in Europe—the company opened its network to everyone who needs it. In an emergency, brand loyalty takes a back seat to community support. IV. Tesla's Disaster-Response Playbook 4.1 A Consistent Pattern Tesla's July 2026 relief effort is part of a consistent pattern that has emerged over several years . The company has activated free Supercharging during: Hurricanes in the United States, including across Mississippi and Tennessee following winter storms in February 2026 Floods in Europe and other regions Earthquakes in Japan, including after the Noto Peninsula earthquake in 2024 Wildfires in multiple countries Winter storms and extreme weather events Humanitarian crises , including opening selected charging locations in Europe to support people traveling away from conflict zones The consistency of the response—same format, same @TeslaCharging announcement channel, same one-week window—suggests Tesla has developed a repeatable operational playbook for disaster relief . 4.2 Why Tesla Does It There are multiple motivations behind Tesla's disaster-response program. Practical necessity : In a disaster, electricity is often the first infrastructure to fail. EVs become stranded without charging access. By opening its Supercharger network, Tesla ensures that EV owners—and in Europe, all EV owners—can evacuate and maintain transportation access . Brand loyalty : Disaster relief builds enormous goodwill among Tesla owners. When a company steps up in a crisis, customers remember. This is not cynical marketing—it is genuine community support that also happens to strengthen the brand. Infrastructure as a public good : Tesla has long positioned the Supercharger network as more than a competitive advantage. It is part of the company's mission to accelerate the world's transition to sustainable energy. Providing free charging during disasters aligns with that mission. Regulatory and political goodwill : By demonstrating that EV infrastructure can serve public safety needs, Tesla builds credibility with regulators and policymakers who might otherwise view the company with skepticism. 4.3 The EV Advantage in Disasters There is a deeper logic to Tesla's disaster-response efforts that is worth noting for EV owners. During power outages, EVs can serve as mobile power sources. The ability to charge an EV during a disaster means the vehicle can provide not just transportation but also climate control and, with bidirectional charging capabilities, power for essential devices. As one Japanese commentator noted, "For EVs that can secure power and air conditioning inside the vehicle, free fast charging is a strong support for evacuation life" . The ability to keep a vehicle charged during an evacuation or extended power outage is not a luxury—it is a lifeline. V. What This Means for Tesla Owners 5.1 Practical Guidance For Tesla owners in affected regions, the relief program requires no special action. The Supercharger session cost will show as zero during the relief window at the named stations . No promo code, account change, or special activation is required. Owners should check the Tesla app's charging map, filter for the named stations, and simply plug in . The relief window closes at midnight on August 5, 2026 . 5.2 What This Says About Tesla's Network Tesla's disaster-response program highlights several strengths of the Supercharger network: Reliability : Tesla can activate free charging across hundreds of stations with a single announcement. The network is centrally managed and consistently maintained. Coverage : The network spans continents. When a disaster strikes in Japan, France, or Spain, Tesla has stations in the affected areas. Flexibility : Tesla can restrict relief to specific stations in specific regions, ensuring that the program targets those who need it most. Openness : In Europe, where the network is already open to non-Tesla EVs, Tesla extended relief to all drivers. This demonstrates that the company's commitment to sustainability transcends brand boundaries. 5.3 Brand Pride and Community For Tesla owners, these disaster-relief efforts are a source of pride. When Tesla steps up during a crisis, it reflects well on the entire community of owners. The company is not just selling cars—it is building infrastructure that serves the public good. This is not a small thing. In an era when many corporations are criticized for putting profits before people, Tesla's disaster-response program stands out as a genuine contribution to community resilience. Conclusion Tesla's July 2026 free Supercharging activation in Japan, France, and Spain is the latest chapter in a consistent pattern of disaster response. In Japan, ten Supercharger stations across Kyushu were opened following a magnitude-7 earthquake. In France and Spain, stations in wildfire-affected regions were made free—and in a significant move, opened to all EV owners, not just Tesla drivers. This is not marketing. It is infrastructure serving its highest purpose: helping communities in crisis. For Tesla owners, it is a reminder that they are part of something larger than a car company. They are part of a network that can provide real help when it matters most. The Supercharger network has always been Tesla's greatest competitive advantage. But in moments of crisis, it becomes something more: a public utility, a lifeline, and a demonstration of what sustainable transportation can achieve. FAQ Q: When does the free Supercharging relief period run? A: From midnight on July 29 through midnight on August 5, 2026 . Q: Which countries are included in the relief program? A: Japan, France, and Spain . Q: How many Supercharger stations are included in Japan? A: Ten stations across five prefectures in Kyushu: Kitakyushu, Fukuoka (two locations plus Hakataeki Minami), Oita, Kumamoto, Miyazaki, and Kagoshima . Q: Which locations are included in France? A: Arès, Biganos, Mérignac, Bordeaux Lac, and Bègles—all in the Bordeaux region . Q: Which locations are included in Spain? A: Castellón, Sagunto, Fuenlabrada, and Majadahonda . Q: Are non-Tesla EVs eligible for free charging? A: Yes, in France and Spain. The European locations are open to all EV owners regardless of brand . In Japan, the stations are Tesla-only . Q: Do I need a promo code or special activation? A: No. The session cost will show as zero at the named stations during the relief window . Q: Has Tesla done this before? A: Yes. Tesla has a consistent track record of offering free Supercharging during hurricanes, floods, wildfires, earthquakes, and other emergencies around the world . Q: What should I do if I'm in an affected area? A: Check the Tesla app's charging map, filter for the named stations, and plug in. The charging will be free . Q: How long will the free charging last? A: Through midnight on August 5, 2026.

title: Wandering the Oregon Woods in a Tired, Good Truck
summary: I seem to have a particularly drug-resistant strain of terrier-chihuahua, so as July 4th approached and I considered my options to remove little Bowie from the endless whiz-bang-booms that are his greatest terror, I broached to my kids the idea of a backpacking trip to a lake. body_text: I seem to have a particularly drug-resistant strain of terrier-chihuahua, so as July 4th approached and I considered my options to remove little Bowie from the endless whiz-bang-booms that are his greatest terror, I broached to my kids the idea of a backpacking trip to a lake. That got me nothing but hems, haws, and exaggerated eye rolling. “What if we drove Sally to the lake instead?” I then suggested. “Do some car camping?” At the mention of utilizing the Xterra they had inexplicably named several years ago, I got zero pushback. They were in. So began the search for a lake that required a truck to get there. Badger Lake sits at the bottom of a glacial cirque in the middle of the 29,000-acre Badger Creek Wilderness , just east of Oregon’s Mt. Hood. It was designated as a wilderness area in 1984, and while such places are considered pristine and undeveloped and contain nothing manmade, the 40-acre lake was dammed in the 1950s, and a rugged two-track spur, Forest Road 140, wanders four miles down to it. As a result, the road and the dam exist as a sort of long, skinny thumb hitchhiking their way into the wilderness. FR 140 curls down into the Badger Creek Wilderness to the lake. Gaia GPS Because the best laid plans of mice and men are almost always disrupted by a failure to get your work done early ahead of a holiday weekend so you can get your groceries, load the cooler, pack the rig, and get out of town with plenty of afternoon sunshine, it was 6:30 before we got on the road. Thankfully, here above the 45th parallel, that still gave us a good two-and-a-half hours of light for our three-hour drive. Mine is not the overlander du jour, replete with light bars and spotlights and ditch lights and probably some other lights I’m not aware of, so I didn’t necessarily want to navigate the woods in the dark, although secretly I knew it’d be fun and we’d be fine. More concerning was the campground at the lake on July 4 weekend: With just four sites, each on a first-come basis, after a long trek into the forest, I really wanted to make sure we got one. Off the main highway, then the secondary highway, we followed Forest Road 4890 for a few miles. Just about every forest road in these parts is an old logging road dating back to the 1950s or so, and 4890 is a winding, climbing, paved single-lane I’ve driven several times over the years. And it always, always , leads me to imagine taking it on as a tarmac stage at 100 mph in a Martini-liveried Lancia—until my inevitable spectacular crash. We arrived at an intersection, and there we took a sharp left onto the unpaved 4891, a road I’ve never driven, and were immediately confronted by two signs: One told us we had 11 miles to Badger Lake, while another, large and bright yellow read: TRAILERS AND BUSES PROHIBITED AT BADGER LAKE ROAD 48601140. Stefan Lombard I aired down my tires to 17 psi, and so began the steady, slow-rolling, carom from rock to rock up the trail. North, roughly, with the sun on our left and still hot through the firs. It was about 8 p.m. and we were doing great; Google Maps told me we’d be at the lake in an hour… And we would have, too, if it weren’t for that meddling F-350! We were halfway down the spur road to the lake when we came upon it, just two miles to go and still in daylight. The Nissan’s high clearance and squishy, grippy Falken Wildpeaks had rendered 4WD unnecessary, and the constant bucking, the squeaks and groans, and the oh-well! hard knocks off the bump stops elicited nothing but whoops and giggles as we’d motored along. We’ve had some great adventures in this machine over the years, and all of the above, giggles included, are a familiar, welcome accompaniment. But then there it was, all 21 feet and 7.3 diesel-y liters of an OBS crew cab long bed. The only thing that could have made it any bigger, in fact, would have been a dually rear end. Or a trailer. Dead slow ahead, hard to port… Stefan Lombard While it’s no Wrangler, a first-generation Xterra is a nimble creature , and its 35-foot turning radius is the kind of thing a fella can be proud of. By which I simply mean: It is easily maneuvered down tight, twisty, rutted, two-tracks that sometimes zig and zag sharply between the sawed ends of large fallen trees, and you’re rarely at risk of holding people up. Something four-thousandths of a mile long, with a 60-foot turning radius, on the other hand, is another creature entirely. This was very much a one-way road, with no place for them to pull off and no place for us to get around, so there we were. Resigned to idle along for the duration at a sub-2-mph pace, I put the truck into 4Lo, which is as close to Level 1 autonomy as Sally the Xterra gets. Google Maps then got very confused, constantly trying to reconfigure our time to destination and effectively scratching its head while wondering how we possibly hadn’t arrived yet. Darkness fell in the forest. Real darkness, the nighttime kind. I’d had my headlights on the whole day but now switched them off so as not to annoy the people annoying me. And it was fine, of course—we would get there. Then, in a literal flash, Johnny Brodude arrived on the scene, hot on my six in a TRD Tacoma bedazzled with all the lights I lacked, possibly all the lights in the known universe. Certainly enough lights shining with enough impatient intensity to elicit a firm middle finger from the guy commanding the carrier in front of me. “Great,” said my oldest kid. “Just great.” Finally, though, after being so agonizingly close for so long, we all arrived at the lake. The Ford and I pulled into a small gravel lot. The Tacoma raced around us and off down a little road that fronted the dam. We turned around in the lot and backtracked to another road I’d sort of made out on the way in, and there, before us in the dark, was an empty campsite. Which was great, because while I’d been eyeing potential places we might retreat to in case the place was already full, I really didn’t want to drive back up that road to one. This was a lake trip, dammit. Stefan Lombard Stefan Lombard Stefan Lombard We read, we napped, we looked at the lake but never ventured in. We then proceeded to hang out in camp just about all weekend. Turns out none of us had a great urge to swim, and we had tiny Badger Creek flowing past our site, which was perfect for cooling off. Instead we read, played games, talked, napped, stuffed our faces. It was perfect. On Saturday the 4th, my friend Collin joined us with his giant lumbering goldendoodle, Abby. His last two cars have been a leased Honda Accord and a leased Hyundai Ioniq 6, but late last year he got himself a Chevy Colorado ZR2. “Are you leasing this thing, too?” I asked him. “Bought it,” he said. “Because I knew I wanted to do this kind of stuff.” Stefan Lombard Stefan Lombard For our purposes on the 4th, “the stuff” included all of us piling into the Chevy for a twilight drive up to a vantage point I’d been eyeballing on the map, with the goal of watching the sunset, making dinner, then looking for silent fireworks in the distance. The ride in the ZR2 was noticeably less groany and squeaky, of course, the truck’s luxe Multimatic DSSV dampers essentially soaking up everything that would pitch the Xterra’s ancient leaf setup this way and that. I rode shotgun with equal parts envy and disgust at the ease of it all. On the way, the white Chevy got a liberal dose of squealing trail stripes down both sides, not exactly something you’d want to deal with on your lease return. The bombs bursting in air… Or the sun setting behind Mt. Hood, anyway, which was glorious in its own way. Stefan Lombard Looking south from our perch toward Madras, Redmond, and Bend, with Mt. Jefferson between the trees. Collin Elsea To the north lay Mt. Adams, with Rainier beyond. Stefan Lombard The evening proved everything we’d hoped it would be, though certainly the fireworks of Madras, Redmond, and Bend—50, 75, and 90 miles from us as the crow flies—were less spectacular than I imagined they might be. Far less spectacular than my Lancia shunt, that’s for sure. But the rest of it—clear views not just of Mt. Hood, but of Mounts Adams and Rainier to the north, and of Jefferson, Three-Fingered Jack, Three Sisters, Broken Top, and Bachelor stretching out far to the south—that was unforgettable. Dehydrated chicken and mashed potatoes? Also not bad. In the morning we broke camp in no great hurry, and some part of me jumped for joy when the Xterra started right up. It’s never given me any reason to suspect it wouldn’t (except when the starter went out last year, which, OK, fine), but who among us doesn’t share that thought ( C’mon, baby!), particularly when you’re far from home? Collin had come in from a different direction than we had, and once out of the wilderness area we followed him. This put us onto Forest Road 3550, which, unbeknownst to me, turned out to be Bennett Pass Road, a one-lane relic of 1930s CCC work that rides atop a ridge at 5000 feet and includes a section known locally as the “Terrible Traverse” for its wintertime susceptibility to avalanches. Felix Lombard Stefan Lombard Stefan Lombard Stefan Lombard Felix Lombard Felix Lombard Stefan Lombard When we reached the highway, we parted ways. On the drive home, I ran the Xterra’s A/C for the first time, and it even sort of worked. My love for this truck comes and goes as my wandering eyes find cheap chunks of steel I might replace it with. I have no need to replace it, but there’s always that classifieds itch. Mostly, it sits in my driveway, where it gets stellar fuel economy, until it’s time for an adventure, when it gets terrible fuel economy. Still, I can’t help being grateful for it. Our holiday excursion was a wonderful reminder of what it does and where it can take us. The post Wandering the Oregon Woods in a Tired, Good Truck appeared first on Hagerty Media .

title: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Becomes Fastest Growing on Record: What You Need to Know

body_text: The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is facing one of its most significant public health emergencies in recent history as the latest Ebola outbreak continues to spread rapidly. Health officials have described the epidemic as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, raising concerns among international health organizations and humanitarian agencies. With thousands of confirmed infections and a rising death toll, authorities are working to contain the virus while dealing with limited resources, healthcare worker shortages, and logistical challenges. The outbreak has also highlighted the urgent need for improved surveillance, access to healthcare, and continued investment in vaccine research. Latest Situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo Health authorities have reported more than 3,000 confirmed Ebola cases since the outbreak was declared in May 2026. More than 1,400 deaths have also been recorded, making it one of the deadliest Ebola outbreaks in recent years. According to health officials, the current outbreak has reached key milestones much faster than previous epidemics. Experts say the speed of transmission has made it increasingly difficult for response teams to identify, isolate, and monitor infected individuals before further spread occurs. The outbreak is affecting several provinces across eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where healthcare systems are already under significant pressure. Why Experts Are Concerned One of the biggest concerns is that many newly confirmed infections cannot be linked to previously identified transmission chains. This means health officials are discovering cases without knowing exactly where the infection originated. When transmission occurs outside known contact networks, it becomes much harder to interrupt the spread of the virus. Contact tracing remains one of the most effective Ebola control measures, but it depends on quickly identifying infected individuals and everyone they have interacted with. The World Health Organization has also indicated that the actual number of infections could be higher than officially reported because some cases may go undetected in remote communities. Healthcare Worker Challenges Efforts to control the outbreak have been complicated by labor disputes involving healthcare workers. Reports indicate that staff at an Ebola treatment center temporarily stopped working due to concerns over unpaid bonuses, while employees at another major hospital also raised concerns regarding delayed salaries. Healthcare workers are essential during infectious disease outbreaks. Any disruption to treatment services can affect patient care, disease surveillance, laboratory testing, and emergency response operations. International organizations continue working alongside local authorities to restore services and strengthen outbreak response efforts. Understanding the Bundibugyo Ebola Virus The current outbreak has been linked to the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus. Unlike the Zaire strain responsible for several previous outbreaks, the Bundibugyo variant has fewer approved medical countermeasures available. Researchers continue studying vaccines and treatments that may help protect against this particular strain. While previous Ebola vaccines have proven effective against certain virus species, scientists continue evaluating additional vaccines that target broader protection. How Ebola Spreads Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials. People may become infected through contact with: Blood Saliva Vomit Urine Feces Sweat Semen Contaminated medical equipment Infected animals The virus does not spread through casual contact or through the air like influenza or COVID-19. Individuals who have died from Ebola can also remain infectious, which is why safe burial practices are considered an essential part of outbreak control. Ebola Symptoms Symptoms usually develop between two and 21 days after exposure. Early symptoms often include: High fever Severe headache Muscle pain Joint pain Weakness Sore throat As the illness progresses, patients may experience: Vomiting Diarrhea Abdominal pain Skin rash Kidney problems Liver problems Internal or external bleeding in severe cases Early diagnosis and supportive medical care can significantly improve a patient's chances of survival. Experimental Vaccines Offer Hope Although there is currently no widely approved vaccine specifically targeting the Bundibugyo strain, researchers continue making progress. Scientists have recently begun testing an experimental vaccine designed using technology similar to vaccine platforms used during the COVID-19 pandemic. Clinical trials are intended to evaluate the vaccine's safety and effectiveness before it becomes available for wider use. While these studies represent an encouraging step forward, experts caution that additional research is still required. International Response Global health organizations, including the World Health Organization (WHO), Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), and humanitarian partners, are supporting the DRC's response. Current priorities include: Identifying new infections quickly Expanding laboratory testing Isolating confirmed patients Tracing close contacts Educating communities Improving infection prevention Supporting healthcare facilities Public health experts emphasize that community cooperation remains one of the most important factors in slowing transmission. Can Ebola Spread Beyond the Region? Although Ebola outbreaks attract worldwide attention, the overall risk of international spread remains relatively low when appropriate public health measures are implemented. Countries maintain surveillance systems at airports, healthcare facilities, and border crossings to rapidly identify potential imported cases. Travelers returning from affected regions are advised to follow official public health guidance and seek medical attention if symptoms develop after potential exposure. The Importance of Continued Investment The current outbreak demonstrates how infectious diseases can quickly overwhelm healthcare systems when resources are limited. Experts continue calling for increased funding to support: Vaccine development Medical research Healthcare infrastructure Disease surveillance Emergency preparedness Healthcare worker training Long-term investment in public health systems can help countries respond more effectively to future outbreaks while reducing the risk of widespread transmission. Final Thoughts The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains a major public health challenge. While response teams continue working to contain the virus, the rapid growth of confirmed cases highlights the importance of early detection, community engagement, and international cooperation. Advances in vaccine research and improved outbreak response strategies offer hope for the future, but sustained investment and coordinated action will remain essential in bringing the current epidemic under control. Frequently Asked Questions What causes Ebola? Ebola is caused by viruses belonging to the Ebolavirus genus. Infection occurs through direct contact with infected bodily fluids or contaminated materials. What are the first symptoms of Ebola? Early symptoms typically include fever, headache, muscle aches, weakness, and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhea in many cases. Is there a cure for Ebola? There is no universal cure for every Ebola virus species. However, supportive medical care and some approved treatments exist for certain Ebola strains, while research continues for others. Can Ebola be prevented? Preventive measures include avoiding contact with infected bodily fluids, practicing proper infection control, safe burial procedures, and vaccination where approved vaccines are available. Sources World Health Organization (WHO) Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) Democratic Republic of Congo Ministry of Health Reuters Associated Press (AP) BBC News Disclaimer This article is intended for informational and educational purposes only. It should not be considered medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Information about disease outbreaks may change as new data becomes available. Always consult official public health authorities such as the World Health Organization (WHO), your local health department, or a qualified healthcare professional for the latest guidance and recommendations.
